Found it. The `formatSummitDate` function in `MountainCard.tsx` (line 90-100) tries to parse the date string with `new Date(dateStr)`. The date is stored as `"January 15, 2026"` which some mobile JS engines can't parse, resulting in "Invalid Date" → "INVALID DATE NaN, NaN".

The fix is simple — since the date is already stored as a formatted string, just display it directly instead of re-parsing it.

The issue was in the `formatSummitDate` function in `MountainCard.tsx`. It was using `new Date(dateStr)` to parse dates stored as strings like `"January 15, 2026"`, which many mobile JS engines can't parse — resulting in "INVALID DATE NaN, NaN".

I replaced it with a simple regex-based parser that extracts the month, day, and year directly from the stored string and formats it without relying on `new Date()`. This works reliably across all platforms.
